column4: Cooperative Development Program (CDP)
column6:
The Cooperative Development Program (CDP) is the flagship program of the Cooperative Development Authority (CDA) designed to advance the viability, competitiveness, and sustainable growth of cooperatives nationwide. Anchored on the CDA’s statutory mandate to promote cooperatives as instruments of equity, social justice, and economic development, the CDP provides an enabling environment that supports the holistic development of cooperative organizations.

The program focuses on strengthening the institutional capacity of cooperatives by delivering technical and professional assistance, capacity-building interventions, and entrepreneurial development support necessary for their efficient operations and long-term sustainability. It encompasses capability-building initiatives for officers and members, skills development programs, mandatory trainings, coaching and mentoring, and specialized support aligned with the cooperative’s development stage and needs.

Through the CDP, the Authority formulates and implements integrated and comprehensive plans for cooperative growth, particularly geared toward enhancing membership participation, improving governance and management practices, and empowering micro and small cooperatives, which constitute the majority of registered cooperatives in the country. The program also facilitates cooperatives’ compliance with reportorial requirements, linkage to markets and livelihood opportunities, and access to financial and enterprise support mechanisms.

The CDP is operationalized through a suite of developmental interventions and support programs, which include, but are not limited to:

a) Handholding Program
b) Provision of Technical Assistance on Cooperative Development
c) Koop Kapatid Program
d) Coop-Biz Enterprise Development Program
e) Financial Assistance Program to Cooperatives
f) Pag-abot Program Realization Through Cooperatives
g) Merger and Consolidation Program

Collectively, these initiatives aim to build strong, resilient, and inclusive cooperatives capable of contributing meaningfully to national and local socioeconomic development.

column4: Completion of Five (5) Storey Technohub Building, KIST Park
column6:
The project involves the completion of the Five (5) Storey Technohub at the Batangas State University – Knowledge, Innovation, and Science Technology (KIST) Park in Alangilan, Batangas City, a key facility within the first PEZA-registered KIST Park in the country designed to support industrial research and development, promote innovation-driven enterprises, and strengthen academe–industry partnerships. With a total project area of 11,268.50 square meters, the project aims to complete all remaining unperformed works to fully deliver a functional, safe, and operational Technology Hub Building. The project is being implemented in three phases: Phase 1, which involved structural and civil works up to the second floor, has been completed; Phase 2, which includes the continuation of structural works for the upper floors together with the installation of electrical, plumbing, and fire protection systems, is currently ongoing; and Completion Phase will cover all remaining architectural, finishing, and MEPF works needed to achieve full operational readiness. Once fully completed, the building will also provide locator spaces for technology-driven enterprises, startups, and industry partners, supporting the University’s vision to advance technological innovation and contribute to the country’s development toward a knowledge-intensive economy.

The facility will include administrative offices such as one (1) Administration Office, one (1) Laboratory Office, and one (1) ICT Service Area; academic, innovation, and professional development spaces including one (1) Ideation Hall, one (1) Technology Showroom, one (1) Validation Space and BMC Arena, one (1) Co-working Space, one (1) Innovation Huddle Space, one (1) Line Agency Shared Service Facility, one (1) Pitch-to-the-World Room, one (1) Control and Audio-Visual Room, multiple Meeting Rooms, three (3) Breakout Rooms, and Function Halls; student, startup, and public support areas comprising one (1) Foyer with Water Feature, one (1) Main Lobby with Lounge and Reception, one (1) Recreation Area, one (1) View Deck, one (1) Snack Bar Area, four (4) Dining/Food Stall Areas, Common Pantries, Leasable Spaces, Customizable Spaces, one (1) Bank Space, and Male/Female Transient and Shower Rooms; building services and utility spaces such as six (6) Electrical Rooms, five (5) Mechanical Rooms, one (1) Utility Room, one (1) Equipment Storage Room, one (1) Pipe Chase Area, and Service Access Areas; circulation and access components including one (1) Escalator Lobby, six (6) Elevator Lobbies, six (6) Main and Service Stairs, six (6) Fire Exits, and multiple Hallways; and sanitary facilities consisting of five (5) Male Restrooms, five (5) Female Restrooms, and five (5) PWD Toilets distributed across all floors, providing a comprehensive environment for innovation, collaboration, and professional engagement.

column4: ICT Industry Development Program
column5: Department of Information and Communications Technology
column6:
Through Republic Act 10844, the Department of Information and
Communications Technology (DICT) was established to be the primary
policy, planning, coordinating, implementing, and administrative entity of the Executive Branch of the government that will plan, develop, and promote the national ICT development agenda.

Among its functions is to ensure the sustainable growth of Philippine
ICT-enabled industries and services resulting in the creation of more career opportunities for Filipino men and women. To fulfill this mission, the DICT developed its ICT Industry Development Program, which aims to lead and manage the development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of ICT initiatives in the country.
The ICT Industry Development Program has six (6) sub-programs handled by the ICT Industry Benchmarking and Promotions Division (IIBPD) and the ICT Industry Ecosystem Development Division (IIEDD). 

The sub programs are as follows:
1. DSDAP: Digital Startup Development and Acceleration Program
2. LIFT: Leveraging the IT-BPM Industry and Fostering Local Talents
3. EPIC: Empowering, Promoting, and Invigorating the Digital
Creative Industry
4. SET PH: Stimulating the Growth of Emerging Technologies in the
Philippines
5. DCP: Digital Cities Program
6. EDGE PH: Empowering Digital Workers of the Gig Industry
Ecosystem in the Philippines

Objectives:
Aligned with the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028, the ICT Industry Development Program primarily aims to improve the country’s stance in the global digital economy by supporting ICT industry development to advance digital transformation and economic growth.

In collaboration with relevant organizations, agencies, and associations in the ICT sector, the ICT Industry Development Program has the following specific
objectives:
1. Develop gender-responsive and inclusive institutional development
programs for ICT Industry stakeholders and key players;
2. Conduct relevant and timely research and development programs to keep abreast with the industry innovations and trends;3. Provide strategic, holistic, and transformative awareness and advocacy
opportunities in the ICT Industry to Filipino men and women as well as
showcase Filipino talent to ensure Philippines’ stature as a leading nation for ICT-enabled services;
4. Showcase local innovative potentials and ICT-enables services towards global synergetic opportunities; and
5. Establish institutionalized partnerships and linkages for the sustainable growth of the ICT Industry.
Sectors Served and its Beneficiaries
The ICT Industry Program serves the associations, organizations, male and female workers, and industry partners in the ICT and ICT Enabled Services sectors.

column4: SEDA Pilipinas: Integrating the Regional Silk Value Chain to Enable Compliance with the Philippine Tropical Fabrics Law (RA 9242) and for the Creative Industries
column6: Silk is a significant textile material for the textiles, garment, fashion, and creative industries. Reaching the collective maximum of 6.3 tons of raw silk for its conversion to 177,000 meters of silk fabrics starting in the year 2026 is possible upon full operation of the silk processing complements and the full backup by the stakeholders and partners in the establishment of 150 silk cocoon production sites within and outside the Regions of the Cordillera, Western Visayas, and Northern Mindanao. Republic Act No. 10644 (RA 10644) otherwise known as the “Go Negosyo Act,” seeks to strengthen MSMEs to create more job opportunities in the country.
The Program started in 2014, with 5 Centers established in the islands of Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. Since then, more Centers have been set up nationwide which are located in strategic areas convenient for the existing and would-be entrepreneurs, such as DTI offices, Local Government Units (LGU), academe, Non-Government Organizations (NGOs), and malls.  They bring ease of doing business closer to MSMEs in all regions and help stimulate entrepreneurship development as MSMEs contribute substantially in driving the Philippine economy.
To date, 1,417 Negosyo Centers (NCs) were already established.

column4: Tatak Pinoy Strategy (TPS) Program under Republic Act No. 11981 or the Tatak Pinoy Act
column6:
The Tatak Pinoy Strategy Program (TPSP) is a comprehensive and dynamic initiative that epitomizes and implements the provisions of the Tatak Pinoy (Proudly Filipino) Act (RA No. 11981).  The program aims to enhance the productivity and competitiveness of our industries, produce and trade a diverse array of more complex and higher quality products and services, create high-paying jobs, and ultimately, increase the country's economic complexity and achieve a robust and vibrant economy. It adopts a comprehensive, multi - sectoral approach based on the pillars of the Tatak Pinoy Act (TPA), namely: (i) human resources; (ii) infrastructure; (iii) technology and innovation; (iv) investments; and (v) sound financial management.

Through the TPSP, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) aims to implement initiatives that enhance the country's economic complexity and competitiveness in the global market. These initiatives are expected to yield tangible economic benefits, such as increasing incomes and living standards of Filipino families; reversing the brain drain or the outflow of Filipino talent, expertise, and know-how; and promoting a wider geographical spread of economic prosperity, especially in less developed areas and disadvantaged sectors. The program represents a strategic step towards positioning the Philippines as a hub of innovation and quality in the international arena.
The TPSP is composed of six (6) components complementing the mentioned pillars of the TPA, which are as follows:
1.	Technology and Innovation Program Component 
Current initiatives under the Technology and Innovation component include the National AI Strategy Roadmap 2.0 and the Center for Artificial Intelligence Research (CAIR). CAIR provides a space for data scientists and researchers to conduct AI research for various industries. The Tatak Pinoy Industry 4.0 Pilot Factory and Learning Academy serves as a model hub for training and research on Industry 4.0 applications. These projects are supported by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) through the PRISTINE Project.

2.	Human Resource Program Component
This component includes the AI and Digital Transformation Upskilling Program for SMEs to help stakeholders use Industry 4.0 technologies. It features SIRI Assessment Training and Certification for local workers. Last April, DTI, in partnership with International Centre for Industrial Transformation (INCIT) and the Asian Development Bank (ADB), conducted SIRI training to equip assessors with the skills to guide manufacturing companies in adopting Industry 4.0.

3.	Investments Program Component 
One of the emerging technologies being explored under this component is the establishment of a Wafer Fabrication Facility, a semiconductor processing facility, which turns wafers into integrated circuits. To this end, a feasibility study for Wafer Fabrication Facility and Integrated Circuit Design Laboratory will be conducted to determine the country’s readiness for this facility, including capabilities in semiconductor manufacturing, electronic component design, and integration of emerging technologies, as well as to assess the supply chain requirements to support the facility.

4.	Market Access Program
This includes market access interventions as one of its priority components to help address the coordination, institutional, and information asymmetry challenges that prevent the Philippine economy from acquiring a comparative advantage in new products and services and from upgrading and expanding its productive capabilities. In line with this, the government will be organizing and participating in local or international fairs/shows, trade, investment, or innovation missions, business matching events, and other similar activities to enable and support the promotion and growth of diversified, sophisticated, and quality Philippine products and services of a “Proudly Filipino” brand.
 
5.	Marketing and Promotions Component
The DTI currently conducts a series of Tatak Pinoy Act (TPA) Fora and Industry Consultations which aim to introduce the newly-enacted law to our stakeholders and, at the same time, engage them in productive discussions on the fundamental aspects of the Act and its vision to elevate the Philippine industries in the global arena. 

A Digital Advocacy campaign, which includes the TPA Promotional Video and Microsite Development, is also in the pipeline to introduce the Tatak Pinoy as a holistic and strategic approach to Philippine industrialization. Lastly, a logo competition is also underway to craft a Tatak Pinoy logo that symbolizes the program’s core mission: to boost the visibility of local products and services, support Filipino industries, enterprises, innovators, and artisans, and enhance our economic performance and cultural prominence on the global stage. 

6.	Policy Development Program Component
This includes the formulation of the Multi-Year Tatak Pinoy Strategy, which is being conducted in partnership with the PricewaterhouseCoopers Philippines (PwC Philippines) and the World Bank. Other initiatives under this pillar include the Development of the Tatak Pinoy List of Products and Services with Preference and Priority in Government Procurement which aims to create a list of projects and services aligned with target key sectors that will be promoted for domestic manufacture through preferential access in procurement. 
The department aims to continue and expand these initiatives to support a sustained diversification and sophistication of Philippine products and services, and develop an enabling environment for innovative enterprises.

column4: Establishment of the Investments Assistance Center of Northern Mindanao
column6:
Northern Mindanao has emerged as a strategic investment destination and supported by its proximity to raw material, a skilled labor force, and recent infrastructural developments. The ERP systems will help SMEs lower operational costs by automating manual tasks, reducing redundant processes, and optimizing resource allocation. This initiative
has the potential to showcase how SMEs can achieve faster return on investments by focusing on high-impact areas like inventory control, financial management, and customer relations management.

Subsequently, to support the implementation of Sections 18 (Product Standards) and 19 (Product Registration) of the law, the DTI through BPS, issued a Technical Regulation for Vape and Heated Tobacco Products (HTP) to ensure that these vaporized nicotine and non-nicotine products conform to the requirements of the relevant Philippine National Standards.

column4: Building a Sustainable Future: Integrating Halal Education and Economic Upliftment for Muslim Filipinos in North Luzon, SOCCSKSARGEN, and Davao
column6:
This initiative, spearheaded by the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos (NCMF), aims to promote sustainable development and inclusive economic empowerment for Muslim Filipino communities
by focusing on four interrelated programs. These programs are
designed to uplift local enterprises, improve Halal literacy, and
enhance market access in line with the NCMF's mandate under
Republic Act No. 9997 and the goals of the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028.

The project will be implemented across three regions:
SOCCSKSARGEN, North Luzon, and Davao, and will feature the
following core components:

1. Halal Summit cum Halal Expo and Trade Fair
This flagship event will serve as a convergence platform for local
producers, Halal stakeholders, government agencies, and investors. It aims to showcase Halal-certified products and services, foster investment through one-on-one business matching, and encourage collaboration across sectors. The summit will also provide a venue to discuss industry challenges, pass actionable resolutions, and promote the rich culture and economic potential of Muslim Filipinos.

2. Proactive Halal Awareness Program. This campaign will focus on educating both Muslim and non-Muslim consumers, businesses, and institutions on the principles and
practices of Halal. The program goes beyond dietary guidelines,
highlighting the ethical, hygienic, and lawful aspects of Halal
production and consumption. It aims to strengthen cultural
understanding and open new markets by enhancing trust in Halal certified products.

3. Capacity Training in Promotion and Development of Muslim
Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMES). This program responds to the findings of the Kabuhayan Probinsya (KP) survey, which revealed a strong interest in MSME development among local beneficiaries. The training series will cover business management, marketing strategies, Islamic financial management, and production enhancement. In partnership with local agencies like DTI, DOST, BAFILCO, and KALIPA, this initiative aims to transform budding entrepreneurs into capable and competitive market players.

4. Capacitate Muslim Filipino Entrepreneurs for the Philippine
Halal Industry With the global Halal market rapidly expanding, this component seeks to equip local entrepreneurs with the skills and knowledge to comply with Halal standards, obtain certification, and access Halal financing. The program includes technical training, regulatory compliance guidance, and strategic linkage to both local and international Halal markets-ultimately increasing the number of certified Halal businesses in the country.

These four programs represent a comprehensive and synergized
strategy that addresses both the supply and demand sides of the
Halal economy while fostering a more inclusive, informed, and
economically empowered Muslim Filipino population.

column4: Establishment of Regional Cooperative Training and Development Centers for Capacity Building and Enterprise Innovation (CDA Regions I, III, CAR, NIR, XI, XII, and XIII)

Cooperatives across agriculture, consumer services, marketing, credit, and other sectors remain essential in improving livelihoods and delivering government services at the grassroots level. To address these gaps, CDA proposes the Establishment of Regional Cooperative Training and Development Centers in seven (7) Regions. These Centers will serve as hubs for cooperative education, leadership development, enterprise innovation, research, and digital transformation. Equipped with modern training halls, offices, dormitories, libraries, and marketing facilities, the Centers will expand CDA’s capacity to deliver high-quality, accessible, and sustainable training programs.

Ultimately, the Centers will empower cooperatives, enhance their competitiveness, and strengthen their contribution to inclusive national development.

column4: Revitalization of the Salt Industry in Mindanao
column6:
Salt has been used by humans for thousands of years, from food preservation to seasoning and it is said that the salt’s ability to preserve food was a founding contributor to human civilization.  Apart from being used as a food preservative, salt is also an essential material in the production of agricultural commodities and manufacturing industries. 

As mentioned above, salt is an essential nutrient that plays a vital role in many bodily functions of humans as well as in the production of agricultural commodities and the operation of different industries. Specifically, the salt is known for but not limited to the following benefits:

For Human

a.	Supports healthy digestion: Salt is integrally involved in digestion as the primary substance that kick-starts digestion in the stomach is hydrochloric acid (HCl) which requires the presence of hydrogen and chlorine ions.
b.	Facilitating body movement: Sodium helps propagate the transmission of electrical impulses from the nerves to the muscles, to allow contraction and movement.
c.	Supporting heart health: Sodium ions help in the transmission of electrical impulses so that pacemaker cells are stimulated to transmit signals to cardiac cells to beat.
d.	Preventing iodine deficiency: Salt is often fortified with iodine, which can help prevent iodine deficiency.

For Industry

e.	Chemical industry: Salt is required in the manufacture of many chemicals, including sodium bicarbonate (baking soda), sodium hydroxide (caustic soda), hydrochloric acid, and chlorine.
f.	Food processing: The meat-packing, sausage-making, fish-curing, and food-processing industries use salt as a preservative or seasoning or both.
g.	Textile industry: Industrial salt increases the uptake of dyes, acts as a filler for pigments, and is used as a grinding agent.
h.	Glass and polyester production: Salt is used in the production of glass and polyester.
i.	Oil industry: In the oil industry, salt is used to increase the density of mud and soil, which creates a more safe and efficient drilling rig.
j.	Solar power: Industrial salt acts as a catalyst for many ionic reactions in the production of solar energy.

For Agriculture

Salt is an essential component in the coconut industry. The Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) recommends using rock salt as a fertilizer for fruit-bearing coconut trees. Applying rock salt around the coconut tree, about 1 meter in diameter, during the onset of the rainy season improves the quality of the fruit by thickening the coconut meat by 25%.

The coconut industry is an important sector of agriculture in the Philippines. With 69 out of 82 provinces in the country producing coconut, the industry has a total production area of 3.62 million hectares and provides at least 2.5 million farmers with employment. In 2018, the Philippines had over 347 million fruit-bearing trees and a total production (mt) of 14.7 million (nut terms). Hence, the coconut industry will require around 347,000 metric tons of salt per year to fertilize the 347,000 million fruit-bearing coconut trees, at 1 kilogram per year per tree. The total requirement of salt is expected to eventually reach 850,000 metric tons (worth $42 million) within the next five (5) years.

However, despite its utmost importance for humans, agriculture, and other allied industries to continuously subsist, salt production in the Philippines is waning. Ninety-three percent (93%) of the country’s salt requirement is imported.

Although some of the identified reasons for its vanishing are mostly the lack of institutional development support, the government has continuously failed to address the problem and the scarcity of domestically produced salt has become a recurring predicament. Notwithstanding the fact that the country as an archipelago is ranked 5th in terms of the longest shoreline in Asia with 36,000 kilometers making it conducive for mass production of salt to address the country’s domestic requirement. 

The recent initiative in both houses of Congress to institutionalize the Development of the Salt Industry Project (DSIP) is currently underway to increase salt production and ensure sufficient supply in the country. The DSIP also aims to assist around 100 local salt makers by providing them with the technology they need to develop their methods and practices in salt production. This program, if properly implemented, will not only address the continuing shortage of locally produced salt but will also provide local employment opportunities for salt farmers in rural areas.

The SPDA, as a government-owned and controlled corporation and taking into consideration the availability of real estate assets located in areas that are potential for salt production, the Authority is looking at the DSIP as an opportunity to take part in the massive production of salt particularly in the island of Mindanao. This endeavor will certainly put the Authority as one of the big players in the salt industry roadmap of the country. Similarly, this initiative will likewise allow the Authority to provide employment opportunities in the rural areas at the same time generate revenues that can be used to replicate the same project in other potential areas for salt production in Mindanao.

column4: SME COMPETE+ Project
column6:
The SME COMPETE+ project is a five-year initiative of the DTI, supported by the World Bank, aimed at enhancing the competitiveness of Philippine suppliers and exporters. It addresses the critical challenge of underinvestment in upgrading, which limits long-term competitiveness in domestic, regional, and global markets. The project promotes the adoption of innovative business practices and improved access to financing, market information, quality testing, certification, and digital platforms. Its three outputs are: (i) adoption of ESQ standards and updated technology implemented; (ii) access to quality testing, inspection, and certification services improved; and (iii) access to digital platforms connecting firms to value chains enhanced.

Through these interventions, SME COMPETE+ seeks to strengthen productivity, market access, and integration of Philippine SMEs into higher-value domestic and international markets.
